segment_performance.highlight: Domestic deliveries grew +4% YoY led by automotive and infrastructure steel demand; EBITDA per ton touched ₹14,200.
Blast furnace relining completed; returned to positive operational EBITDA.
Transition to Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) underway; closure of legacy blast furnaces curtailing operating cash burn.
Tubes, wires, and downstream engineering fabrication products.

simple_pointers: **Indian Operations Drive Profitability:** Tata Steel India delivered robust operational EBITDA of **₹6,820 Cr** (19.57% margin), offsetting European restructuring costs.
**Consolidated Net Profit Turns Positive:** PAT rebounded to **₹918 Cr** (+79.65% QoQ; +44.8% YoY), aided by lower coking coal input costs.
**Kalinganagar Phase 2 Commissioning:** Blast furnace expansion at Kalinganagar adds 5 MTPA high-margin capacity, lowering domestic production costs per ton.
**UK Transition Milestones Achieved:** Shut down of loss-making Port Talbot blast furnaces will reduce recurring European cash drain starting late FY27.
**Deleveraging Focus Maintained:** Net debt stood at ₹82,160 Cr; management reaffirmed commitment to annual deleveraging targets.

strengths: 100% captive iron ore security in India shielding domestic operations from international raw material spikes.
Leading market position in automotive flat steel and pre-engineered infrastructure structural sections.
High-efficiency coastal assets with low cost of conversion at Jamshedpur and Kalinganagar.
weaknesses: Ongoing restructuring losses and transition capex in UK operations dragging overall return on equity.
Higher debt-to-equity ratio (net debt ~₹82k Cr) compared to pure domestic peers.
opportunities: Commissioning of 5 MTPA Kalinganagar expansion driving volume growth and economies of scale.
Decarbonization grant support from UK government (£500M) for the green Electric Arc Furnace transition.
threats: Global steel oversupply and surge in cheap Chinese hot-rolled coil exports pressuring domestic steel realization prices.
European carbon border adjustment tax (CBAM) compliance costs on export shipments.
